demonstrated_gap: Seeded as FlagEmbedding/BGE-M3 (coordinator P2). No gap for this requirement was demonstrated. Per the README news, BGE-M3 dates from 2024-01-30. FlagEmbedding's 2026 releases add BGE-Reasoner (reasoning-intensive retrieval, v1.4.0) and Transformers 5 fixes (v1.4.1 and v1.4.2), but no code-retrieval model. The decisive reason is that the layer's measured loss is in the indexing pipeline: SocratiCode scored 0.857/0.721, while the incumbent embedder queried directly scored 0.971/0.853 on the same sealed set. Swapping the embedder does not address that loss, and any embedder swap forces re-embedding into a new collection. BGE-M3's one fit angle is that it appears in vllm-metal's experimental pooling list for Macs. That is covered by the vllm-metal row, which also lists Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, a model with a published MTEB Code v1 score (75.42 in LightOn's table).

demonstrated_gap: Seeded (coordinator P2). No gap for this requirement. HippoRAG 2 is a document-memory framework whose indexing runs LLM OpenIE extraction over every passage. Its API takes an llm_model_name alongside the embedding model, and its reproduction uses gpt-4o-mini or Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct OpenIE, with an offline vLLM example spread over 4 GPUs. It is evaluated on NQ, PopQA, NarrativeQA, MuSiQue and 2Wiki document QA, not on code spans. Its README documents no code-aware chunking and no incremental indexing on file changes. The only GitHub release is v1.0.0 (2025-02-27); the README refers to a 2.0.0a5 alpha. The decisive reason: it would add a generative model to a code index on a single 24 GB GPU already shared with the embedding service, and there is no evidence that doing so improves code retrieval.
comparison_that_would_overturn: A sealed set of multi-hop, cross-file conceptual code questions where SocratiCode's hybrid search and graph tools fail. HippoRAG 2, using a local vLLM LLM and the incumbent embedder, would need to improve source-grounded recall on that set with acceptable index time and GPU memory on the workstation.
evidence: https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG/blob/main/README.md: describes HippoRAG 2 as a memory framework. Usage requires llm_model_name plus embedding_model_name. OpenIE results are provided for gpt-4o-mini and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, and the offline vLLM OpenIE example uses CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3. Evaluation uses NQ, PopQA, NarrativeQA, MuSiQue and 2Wiki. Mentions version 2.0.0a5.

demonstrated_gap: On the layer's sealed 35-question agent-lab set, the winning pipeline (SocratiCode 1.14.0 + Qdrant + Nemotron-3-Embed-1B on vLLM) scored Recall@5 0.857 / MRR 0.721. The same embedder queried directly scored 0.971 / 0.853, so the loss comes from the indexing and ranking pipeline, not the model. SocratiCode's index/watcher recovery is not_established, and all three winners are untested on macos-arm64. ColGREP, the tool in this repository, replaces the three services with one local Rust binary: no server, no Qdrant, no embedding service. It checks for changed files and updates its index on every search, so there is no watcher daemon to recover. It keeps one index per (project, model) and fuses ColBERT MaxSim with FTS5 trigram keyword search by RRF. It ships macOS arm64 binaries with CoreML/Accelerate. Its default models are the Apache-2.0 late-interaction code retrievers LateOn-Code-edge (17M) and LateOn-Code, both trained with PyLate; this row carries the seeded PyLate/ColBERT item. The encoder runs in-process rather than as a service. The layer's overturn clause is outcome-based (sealed-set quality plus latency, memory and lifecycle), so a service-free index qualifies if it wins.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Install colgrep v1.7.0 from the pinned release tarball, checked against its published .sha256, on the WSL workstation. Use the Homebrew or darwin tarball with CoreML on the M5 Pro. Run it on the sealed 35-question agent-lab set and on a new sealed set of identifier-free conceptual questions, with the same Recall@5/MRR line-overlap rule as held-out-recall-benchmark.json. Test both LateOn-Code-edge at the INT8 CPU default and LateOn-Code at FP32. Also measure cold index time, incremental update after a one-file edit, query p50, peak RSS, and whether results match after deleting and rebuilding the index. Adopt as a replacement or Mac complement if it matches or beats SocratiCode's 0.857/0.721 on both sets at lower lifecycle cost. Refute if it trails SocratiCode on the conceptual set, or if the CPU INT8 run reproduces MinishLab's 0.693 rather than LightOn's 0.846 on a Semble-bench subset.
evidence: https://github.com/lightonai/next-plaid/blob/main/README.md: ColGREP is 'a single Rust binary' with 'No server, no API, no dependencies'. demonstrated_gap: Same pipeline and platform gaps as above: SocratiCode 0.857/0.721 against the incumbent embedder's own 0.971/0.853 on the sealed set; watcher recovery not_established; winners untested on macos-arm64. Semble is an MIT library, CLI and MCP server that runs on CPU with no GPU, API key, embedding service or vector database. It combines potion-code-16M-v2 static embeddings (MIT), BM25 and a ranking stage. Its per-repo index is cached in the OS cache folder and invalidated automatically when files change, so recovery means a fast rebuild instead of a watcher and Qdrant restore. Its public pinned benchmark (1,251 queries, 63 repos, 19 languages) reports NDCG@10 of 0.854, against CodeRankEmbed 0.839, ColGREP 0.693, BM25 0.673 and codebase-memory-mcp 0.630. In its ablation the ranking stage adds about 0.16 to 0.17 NDCG. SocratiCode has no such stage: its README documents only dense + BM25 RRF. SocratiCode and the Nemotron embedder were never measured on that benchmark.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Install semble 0.6.1 with `uv tool install` in an isolated prefix. Configure its MCP entry by hand rather than with `semble install`, which also writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions and a sub-agent. Use local paths only. Run it with content set to code and docs on the sealed 35-question set and on a fresh identifier-free conceptual set, on WSL and on the M5 Pro. In the other direction, run SocratiCode 1.15.0 with Nemotron on a pinned subset of semble's public benchmark. Adopt as a replacement or Mac default if it matches or beats SocratiCode's 0.857/0.721 on the sealed sets with lower index time, RSS and restore cost. Refute if its public-bench lead does not carry over to the sealed conceptual set. The public labels were generated by Claude Sonnet 4.6, which also judged them, and v0.6.0 corrected 11 of them.
evidence: https://github.com/MinishLab/semble/blob/main/README.md: 'runs on CPU with no API keys, GPU, or external services required'. Provides an MCP server for Claude Code and Codex, installed with `uv tool install semble`. Indexes are cached per repo in the OS cache folder and 'invalidated automatically when files change'. `semble install` adds AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions and a sub-agent.

https://github.com/MinishLab/semble/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md: 1,251 queries over 63 pinned repos in 19 languages. NDCG@10: semble 0.854, CodeRankEmbed 0.839, ColGREP 0.693, BM25 0.673, ck 0.642, codebase-memory-mcp 0.630. Ablation: ranking lifts BM25 from 0.675 to 0.834 and hybrid reaches 0.854. Queries and labels were generated by Claude Sonnet 4.6, which also judged label quality. All tools ran CPU-only, and SocratiCode is not included.

demonstrated_gap: A concrete challenger for project scoping and watcher correctness: upstream documents per-request project roots and protection against concurrent watchers losing index state. These address unresolved lifecycle requirements, although superiority over SocratiCode remains unmeasured.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare against SocratiCode using frozen questions and a common embedding checkpoint. Measure source-span Recall@5, nDCG@10, latency and memory. Exercise edits, renames, deletions, ignored files, concurrent watchers, interrupted indexing and cross-host restore. Promote only with better retrieval or demonstrably better lifecycle correctness and zero cross-project leakage.
evidence: [README](https://github.com/yoanbernabeu/grepai): documents semantic search, call graphs, MCP, file watching, local Ollama embeddings, Linux/macOS installation and MIT licensing.

demonstrated_gap: Provides a bounded way to test whether token-level late interaction improves conceptual code ranking. Its reranking interface can operate on the existing retriever's candidates without first replacing the durable index. This tests the missing comparative-quality evidence.
comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL RTX 4090, rerank the same frozen top-50 candidates with the documented ColBERT pipeline. Require a positive paired confidence interval for nDCG@10 improvement, no grounded-answer regression, and acceptable added latency and VRAM. Qualify checkpoint licensing first; qualify native Mac execution separately.

demonstrated_gap: The v1.15.0 upgrade addresses a specific lifecycle defect: reading a Qdrant collection before this process's creation completes. It also preserves Qdrant error reasons and delivers MCP log notifications. These justify testing the upgrade without treating incumbency as evidence of retrieval quality.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare 1.14.0 and 1.15.0 under simultaneous startup, delayed collection creation and interrupted initialization, then run watcher and restore checks. Prefer 1.15.0 if it eliminates reproduced races without scope, retrieval, latency or memory regressions. This does not independently establish whole-stack recovery.
